bibliographic.title: AI-driven framework for contract risk automation and compliance in Oracle CPQ
bibliographic.citation_apa: Soma, R. (2026). AI-driven framework for contract risk automation and compliance in Oracle CPQ. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-55942-7

methodology.method_family: prototype framework with structured simulation experiments
methodology.study_design: simulation-validated prototype evaluation against manual legal review and rule-based NLP baselines
methodology.sample_description: corpus of 500 synthetic SaaS contract documents evaluated under identical simulation conditions
methodology.sector: IT and SaaS enterprise contract management and quoting (Oracle CPQ)
methodology.technology_context: Oracle Configure-Price-Quote (CPQ) integrated via REST API event hooks; BERT-based semantic matching; GPT-4 generative module with RAG; compliance benchmarking against GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article presents a simulation-validated AICRIM framework integrating GPT-4 and BERT into Oracle CPQ for contract compliance and risk assessment in regulated SaaS contexts, with explicit AI governance controls (encryption, bias monitoring, audit trails, guardrails, RAG, human legal review gates). It does not describe or evaluate conversational AI, chatbots, agents, or dialogue-based systems, so it is not central evidence for conversational governance but may support adjacent themes of LLM governance, compliance automation, and oversight in regulated enterprise workflows.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python metadata incorrectly classified venue as conference_paper and garbled the title; full-text scope beyond provided excerpts should be verified for any conversational or agentic components and for completeness of governance claims.

appraisal.notes: Strengths include a clearly specified multi-module architecture, defined baselines, reported metrics, and explicit acknowledgment that results are simulation-derived pending real-world validation. Weaknesses include reliance on synthetic contracts, prototype-level status rather than production deployment, and limited detail in the provided text on governance implementation beyond high-level controls.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are internally coherent for a CPQ contract-risk prototype, but confidence is moderated because evidence comes from simulation on synthetic data and the study is not conversational-AI focused; governance relevance is partial and indirect for the review's core scope.

coding.theme: AI governance and compliance automation for generative AI in enterprise contract workflows
coding.subtheme: Non-conversational CPQ risk assessment with governance safeguards
rq_alignment: AI governance in regulated LLM deployments

synthesis.main_claim: AICRIM integrates GPT-4 and BERT into Oracle CPQ to automate real-time contract compliance and risk assessment, achieving reported simulation improvements in error reduction, cycle time, and compliance detection accuracy while embedding governance controls for ethical and auditable deployment.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a prototype-level architectural framework for coupling generative AI, semantic matching, RAG, and an AI governance layer within CPQ workflows for GDPR/HIPAA/ISO 27001-aligned contract review.
synthesis.limitations: Evaluation is simulation-based on 500 synthetic SaaS contracts; results are presented as indicative upper-bound estimates pending real-world validation; the system is a prototype, not a fully deployed production system.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as supporting evidence on technical and operational governance of specific LLMs (GPT-4) in regulated enterprise settings, but not as central evidence on conversational governance because no conversational, dialogue, chatbot, or agent interaction model is described.
